name: Caspian Sea
genZNote: The Caspian is the one on this list that isn't actually connected to the ocean at all — it's the world's largest inland body of water, sea in name only.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & a Geographic Correction
bullets: The world's largest inland body of water, between south-eastern Europe and Central Asia — despite the name, it is fully landlocked and has no connection to any ocean.

Whether it counts as a 'sea' or the world's largest lake is a genuinely debated classification — this app lists it here as a named 'sea' for completeness, while noting it does not connect to open ocean water like every other entry in this section.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan.

sections.heading: 🚢 Resources & Regional Trade
bullets: Holds major oil and natural gas reserves beneath its seabed, making it economically important to all five bordering countries.
Used for regional shipping and ferry routes between bordering countries, though entirely separate from global ocean shipping networks.
Baku (Azerbaijan) is its most significant port city.

sections.heading: 🐟 Ecological Significance
bullets: Historically famous for Caspian Sea sturgeon and caviar production, though sturgeon populations have declined sharply due to overfishing and habitat pressure.
Its water level has been observed shrinking in recent decades, an ongoing environmental concern for the bordering countries.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, fully landlocked between Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
keyFacts: World's largest inland body of water; fully landlocked.
Borders Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan.
commonConfusion: Despite its name, the Caspian Sea has NO connection to any ocean — don't group it with the Black Sea or Mediterranean's connected-sea network.

highYieldFacts: Caspian Sea = world's largest inland/landlocked water body.
Bordered by 5 countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan.
Rich in oil and gas reserves.
commonTraps: A common exam trap: assuming every 'Sea' connects to the ocean — the Caspian is the clearest counterexample.
mustRemember: Caspian Sea = landlocked, world's largest inland water body, no ocean access.
